heart_rate.label: Heart rate
heart_rate.what: Number of heartbeats per minute, measured at rest.
heart_rate.why_in_space: NASA HRP identifies cardiovascular adaptations as a risk: microgravity changes blood circulation and the function of the heart and blood vessels.

bp_systolic.label: Systolic blood pressure
bp_systolic.what: Pressure in the arteries when the heart contracts.
bp_systolic.why_in_space: On the ISS, 24-h ambulatory blood pressure was measured 8-10 mmHg lower than before flight (Norsk et al., 2015). A lower reading in flight is therefore expected, not a warning sign by itself.

bp_diastolic.label: Diastolic blood pressure
bp_diastolic.what: Pressure in the arteries between heartbeats.
bp_diastolic.why_in_space: On the ISS, 24-h ambulatory diastolic pressure was measured about 9 mmHg lower than before flight (Norsk et al., 2015).

glucose.label: Blood glucose
glucose.what: Amount of sugar in the blood.
glucose.why_in_space: NASA HRP identifies the risk of inadequate nutrition during long missions.

temperature.label: Core body temperature
temperature.what: Internal body temperature, measured at rest.
temperature.why_in_space: Resting core temperature rises by about 1 °C over the first 2.5 months on the ISS (Stahn et al., 2017). An Earth-calibrated tool reads that normal adaptation as a fever; this tool follows the expected in-flight curve instead.

sleep_hours.label: Sleep
sleep_hours.what: Amount of sleep in the last 24 hours.
sleep_hours.why_in_space: Astronauts averaged about 6 hours of sleep per night on ISS missions although 8.5 hours were scheduled (Barger et al., 2014).

mood.label: Mood (self-reported)
mood.what: A self-assessment from 1 (very poor) to 5 (very good). This is not a clinical scale.
mood.why_in_space: NASA HRP identifies the risk of behavioral changes related to isolation and confinement.

alertness.label: Alertness (self-reported)
alertness.what: How alert you feel, from 0 (exhausted) to 10 (fully alert). This is not a clinical scale.
alertness.why_in_space: People under chronic sleep restriction are largely unaware of their growing performance deficits (Van Dongen et al., 2003). This self-rating is compared with the objective reaction-time test.

pvt_lapses.label: Vigilance test: lapses
pvt_lapses.what: Number of slow responses (355 ms or more) in the 3-minute reaction-time test (PVT-B).
pvt_lapses.why_in_space: The PVT-B was developed for spaceflight to detect fatigue-related losses of alertness objectively (Basner, Mollicone & Dinges, 2011).

pvt_mean_rt.label: Vigilance test: mean reaction time
pvt_mean_rt.what: Average reaction time in the 3-minute reaction-time test (PVT-B).
pvt_mean_rt.why_in_space: Slower responses are an objective sign of reduced alertness after sleep loss (Basner, Mollicone & Dinges, 2011).
